en: Mayon Volcano in Albay has a six-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone to protect people from sudden lava avalanches.
Living near the Philippine coast requires knowing tsunami evacuation routes because undersea earthquakes can trigger giant, destructive waves.
PAGASA issues Tropical Cyclone Wind Signals to warn Filipinos about expected wind speeds so they can prepare for typhoons.
Avoid swimming in the Pasig River because industrial waste and sewage make the water highly toxic and unsafe for health.
During the dry season, high heat index levels in Manila require students to drink plenty of water to prevent heatstroke.
Clearing stagnant water around your home in the Philippines prevents Aedes aegypti mosquitoes from breeding and spreading the deadly dengue virus.
Hikers climbing Mount Pulag in Benguet must wear thick jackets because the high altitude causes dangerously low nighttime temperatures.
Swimmers at Philippine beaches must watch for rip currents, which are strong underwater channels that can pull people out to sea.
Wearing a mask in Metro Manila protects your lungs from inhaling harmful smoke and dust generated by heavy traffic.
Boiling artesian well water in rural Philippine provinces kills harmful bacteria, making it safe for drinking and preventing waterborne diseases.
Because the Philippines is near the equator, applying sunscreen protects children's skin from severe sunburns caused by high ultraviolet radiation.
Planting trees on the steep slopes of the Cordillera mountains prevents soil erosion and protects villages from deadly landslides during heavy rains.
